proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord + MagicItemMechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: No 'magic_item' kind exists in UnitRecord. The taxonomy defines magic_item_root as a source atom but the surface has no record shape for magic items at all. A MagicItemRecord (with id, name, provenance, description, attunement requirements, rarity) and at least one MagicItemMechanics family are required before any magic item can be honestly encoded.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Wondrous Item, Very Rare (Requires Attunement by a Wizard)

proposed_widenings.name: ability_check resolution phase in ActivationPhase
proposed_widenings.justification: The Unknown Spell property is gated by an Intelligence (Arcana) ability check, not a saving throw. The ability_check atom exists in v4 taxonomy but there is no ActivationPhase variant (nor ClassFeatureMechanics variant) for ability_check resolutions with DC formulas that depend on spell level.
proposed_widenings.evidence: make an Intelligence (Arcana) check (DC 10 plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access effect (runtime-selected, unknown spell from list)
proposed_widenings.justification: The core success outcome is casting a spell not in the caster's repertoire, chosen at activation time, from a class list, at a castable slot level. The grant_spell_access atom exists in v4 taxonomy but there is no surface variant for runtime-selected, activation-time spell access gated by a check result.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can try to cast a level 1+ spell you don't know. The spell must be on the Wizard spell list, it must be of a level you can cast

proposed_widenings.name: random_outcome_table — stochastic failure branch with d100 dispatch
proposed_widenings.justification: On a failed ability check, a d100 table fires with 10 distinct outcome bands, several of which nest further sub-tables (d10, d4, d6). Outcomes include conditions (Stunned, Poisoned, Petrified), creature summoning, object creation, portal opening, and casting a random spell. No surface type or atom models a stochastic dispatch table. Many sub-outcomes are individually dm_agenda (GM chooses portal destination, GM chooses magic item), but the table dispatch itself is a deterministic core mechanic that needs a closed representation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: On a failed check, you fail to cast the spell and a random effect occurs instead, determined by rolling on the following table. [d100 table with 10 bands and nested sub-rolls]

notes: The primary blocker is structural: UnitRecord has no 'magic_item' kind. The secondary mechanics blockers (ability_check gate, grant_spell_access, random failure table) are all independently novel. The 'Spellcasting Focus' property is a passive item property with no combat mechanic — it would also need a passive_property family or similar. The use-count + Short/Long rest reset on the Unknown Spell property does fit existing vocabulary (use_count + short_or_long_rest). The random failure table's sub-outcomes mix partially-encodable mechanics (apply_condition, create_companion) with dm_agenda outcomes (portal destination, magic item selection) — the table itself requires a new stochastic dispatch subgraph even if individual outcome slots delegate to existing atoms.
